title: `structuredContent`
description: A JSON result value returned alongside `content`, conforming to the tool's `outputSchema` when one is declared.
question: Does the agent receive the structured value, or only its text rendering?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: The spec asks servers to mirror structured results into a text block for backwards compatibility. That mirror makes a dropped `structuredContent` invisible: the call still looks successful, and typed data quietly becomes a string the model has to re-parse.

notes.crewai: CrewAI: structuredContent is dropped; only the text mirror reaches the agent.
notes.langchain: LangChain: structuredContent is dropped; only the text mirror reaches the agent.
notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents: structuredContent is dropped; only the text mirror reaches the agent.
notes.pydantic-ai: Pydantic AI: `structuredContent` is returned only when every content part is text, and then in place of the text. A result that also carries an image or audio block loses the typed value and passes only the text mirror.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): execute resolves with the CallToolResult including structuredContent. toModelOutput maps only the `content` list, so the model gets the text blocks and never the typed value. Boundary-dependent: kept at execute, dropped at model_output. With a caller-supplied outputSchema (the `schemas` option), execute returns the validated structuredContent instead; that path was not measured.
notes.ms_agent_framework: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: with the default `tool_result_content="structured_first"` the adapter serializes `structuredContent` to JSON and returns it as one text `Content` in place of the content blocks. No structured value reaches the agent; the complete CallToolResult rides in the function result's `additional_properties` for hosts, which a chat client does not send.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: Every boundary drops `structuredContent`: `ToolResult` holds text and image parts only, and `McpToolAdapter.run_json` returns `result.content` alone.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: `MCPServer.callTool` keeps `structuredContent` on the returned array, but the model never receives it by default: the agent hands over the content blocks. With the non-default `useStructuredContent: true` it hands over `JSON.stringify(structuredContent)` as text instead, which is not the typed value either.
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `_mcp_call_tool_result_to_kernel_contents` converts `content` only; `structuredContent` is discarded at both boundaries.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `FunctionTool._parse_tool_output` has no case for `CallToolResult`, so the `ToolOutput`, and the `ChatMessage(role="tool")` a `FunctionAgent` sends the model, hold one text block: the result's Python repr. `structuredContent` appears in that text, never as a structured value.
notes.pi: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient.callTool` returns `structuredContent`. `toLlmContent` uses it only when the result has no content blocks, as JSON text, so a result with text and structured content reaches the model without the typed value.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: boundary-dependent. The `ToolResult` the Function entrypoint returns keeps `structuredContent` in `metadata['structured_content']`; the tool `Message` the next model turn receives carries the text content only, so the model never gets the structured value.
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): boundary-dependent. The direct `Tool.invoke` return is that JSON string, which the adapter's docstring says to read with `json.loads`; parsed, it keeps every block. The `ChatMessage` an `Agent` hands the next generator turn carries the Tool's return value as one text: the `CallToolResult` JSON from `model_dump_json`. `structuredContent` appears in that text, never as a structured value.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): with `structured_output` left at its default (`False`, the legacy behavior; smolagents warns the default will change), `MCPAdaptTool.forward` returns `content[0]` and never reads `structuredContent`, so only the text mirror reaches the agent. `MCPClient(..., structured_output=True)` returns `structuredContent` instead; that opt-in was not measured.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: with the default `result_mode="text"`, `_convert_mcp_tool_result` returns the text blocks only, so `structuredContent` reaches neither the caller nor a `dspy.ReAct` observation. The documented non-default `from_mcp_tool(..., result_mode="structured")` returns `structuredContent` alone and drops the text.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): the tool is `content_and_artifact`. `structuredContent` goes into the artifact as `mcp_structured_content`, which LangChain keeps app-side; the `ToolMessage` content the model reads, and the `tool.invoke` value, hold only the text mirror.
notes.spring_ai: Spring AI 2.0.1: `structuredContent` is dropped at both boundaries; the agent and a direct `ToolCallback.call` see only the JSON of the content list.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: when a result has `structuredContent`, `MCPTool._run` returns it alone and drops every content block (direct: `y`). The model gets `JSONToolOutput.get_text_content()`, the structured value serialized as one JSON string with no separate field (agent: `n`).
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): depends on the boundary. `agent`: `structuredContent` is serialised as JSON and appended to the text in the `tool` message (`SENTINEL_TEXT_BLOCK\n\n{"count":2,...}`); no structured value reaches the provider. `direct`: `session.rpc.tools.execute` returns `structuredContent` as an object.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient._call_tool_impl` keeps only `content[0]`, returning its `text` when it has one and `str(content[0])` otherwise and never reads `structuredContent`, so only the text mirror reaches the agent.
notes.google_adk_java: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `wrapCallResult` reads only `CallToolResult.content()`; `structuredContent` is dropped. `text_and_structured` returns `{"text_output": [{"text": "SENTINEL_TEXT_BLOCK"}]}` at both boundaries.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: when a result has `structuredContent`, `McpToolExecutor` returns it as `ToolExecutionResult.result()` and sets `resultText` to its Jackson re-serialization. The direct executor therefore yields the structured value (direct: `y`), while the agent's `ToolExecutionResultMessage` carries only that JSON string (agent: `n`).

verdict.detail: structuredContent exists so an agent can consume a result without parsing prose. Where it is dropped, the typed value a server carefully produced is replaced by its own human-readable summary.

summary: structuredContent is the typed value; the text content beside it is a mirror meant for humans. An adapter that hands the agent only the mirror drops the typed value.
